Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Intermittent episodes of right-hand paresthesia (pins and needles), numbness, and transient weakness of the right arm and ipsilateral leg; associated fatigue and nausea.
- History of present illness:
  - Onset: symptoms began approximately 1–2 months ago.
  - Duration/progression: initially episodes occurred maybe weekly to monthly; have increased in frequency to multiple episodes per day. Individual episodes last a few days (reported 3–4 days) and then resolve to baseline.
  - Symptom details:
    - Paresthesia and numbness localized to the right hand.
    - Subjective right arm weakness during episodes.
    - Concurrent transient right leg weakness and intermittent abnormal gait noted by colleague during episodes.
    - During recent episodes (last couple of days) difficulty holding a cup of coffee; drinking slightly more difficult.
    - Sensation of “something in my throat” during episodes.
    - No reported speech difficulty during episodes.
    - No reported visual changes (patient wears glasses).
    - Generalized tiredness, weakness, intermittent nausea, reduced motivation.
  - Currently asymptomatic at time of consultation.
- Past medical history:
  - No chronic illnesses reported.
  - Prior screening (after father's surgery): cholesterol, diabetes, and blood pressure previously checked and reported as "all OK" (no results provided).
- Medications:
  - Aspirin 75 mg once daily — self-initiated. Route not documented.
- Social history:
  - Occupation: medical doctor, plastic surgery.
  - Lives with wife.
  - Non-smoker.
- Allergies:
  - Penicillin.

Objective:
- General/neurological examination: no formal exam findings documented.
- Current state: patient asymptomatic during consultation.
- Imaging/laboratory investigations: none performed or results available in this consultation.
- Other: video connection lost during consultation; remote assessment only.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Transient ischemic attack (TIA) — suspected
   - Assessment or likely diagnosis: Transient ischemic attack (TIA)
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Ischemic stroke (if symptoms are prolonged) — discussed as important alternative if episodes do not resolve
   - Investigations planned:
     - Urgent referral to TIA clinic (referral to be sent immediately)
     - Expected investigations at TIA clinic: carotid artery ultrasound and possible brain imaging (e.g., CT or MRI) as determined by the clinic
   - Treatment planned:
     - No acute medication changes documented in this consultation
     - Advice: attend Emergency Department immediately if symptoms recur and are prolonged (concern for stroke)
     - Advise patient may contact GP/clinic for telephone assessment if symptoms recur
   - Relevant referrals:
     - Urgent TIA clinic referral (hospital to contact patient within ~1–2 days); clinic/PALS contact information to be placed in notes for patient to chase appointment

2. Aspirin use (self-prescribed)
   - Assessment or likely diagnosis: Self-initiated low-dose aspirin use
   - Differential diagnosis: N/A
   - Investigations planned: None documented
   - Treatment planned:
     - No change to medication documented during this consultation
     - Will be reviewed as part of TIA clinic assessment (not explicitly stated as changed in transcript)
   - Relevant referrals: Reviewed in context of TIA clinic referral
